newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire says its helicopter gunships attack rebels.
newsitem.headline: Zaire says its helicopter gunships attack rebels.

text.p: Zaire's armed forces have been using helicopter gunships to attack rebels advancing from the north and east on the strategic third city of Kisangani, a senior defence ministry official said on Saturday.

"Since Wednesday our MI-24 combat helicopter have been conducting raids between Bafwasende and Banalia," a senior defence ministry official told Reuters, adding that rebels had been as close as 130 km (80 miles) to the city.
Kisangani, strategically placed on the Zaire River, is headquarters for the counter-offensive Zaire's army launched on January 20. Rebels leader Laurent Kabila has named it as one of his targets.
The ministry official said the helicopters, flying low, had inflicted heavy casualties on rebel positions. "There were many dead, but we don't have an exact death toll yet," he added.
Banalia is just over 100 km (60 miles) north of Kisangani, the provincial capital of the vast Upper Zaire province.

The official said the army would launch similar raids on other fronts. Government planes launched an air raid on rebel-held towns in the east on Monday, killing up to 19 people according to aid workers.
The ministry official said Zairean soldiers had taken four prisoners of war on Thursday during one clash.
Zaire accuses neighbouring Rwanda, Burundi and Uganda of invading in support of the rebels, a charge all three deny.
